response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack/web software engineer with 13+ years of professional work, but there is essentially no overlap with the core requirements of a Principal Performance Architect for AI accelerators. The resume shows no SoC or IP modeling, no hardware-software co-design, no GPU/SIMD/MIMD architecture work, and no deep-learning training or inference optimization. The closest adjacent experience is low-latency service work in DLang at Sociomantic and some C/C++ at National Instruments, which is application-level rather than silicon-level performance engineering. Education is a BS in Computer Science with sufficient years of experience to meet the formal bar, but the domain expertise required for this principal-level hardware architecture role is absent.
strengths: 13+ years of broad software engineering experience, meeting the BS + 8 years bar
Some low-latency, high-throughput systems work (DLang, async I/O, fibers) and C/C++ exposure
Strong engineering practices, open-source ownership, and public teaching/talks
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, RTL, or hardware architecture experience whatsoever
No deep-learning workload, GPU, or AI accelerator optimization background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack product work, not principal-level silicon performance architecture

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware co-design
No AI accelerator or DNN optimization experience
